correctness.rationale: The n private leaf pairs force gamma≥n, and all originals dominate, so gamma=n. Equality selects exactly one per pair and no subdivision nodes. Each subdivided edge forces at least one original endpoint, precisely the independent-set condition for selected leaves. All minimum-set exchanges are exactly one pair flip along the private edge, yielding both jump and token-slide gamma graphs with Hamming distances. A k-dimensional cube within the hypercube has unique top independent set and k toggled coordinates, giving c_k=Σ_I binom(|I|,k) and cube polynomial I_F(1+q). Vertex-degrees, bipartiteness, girth and parsimonious counting-hardness are proved directly; Greenhill Theorem 3.1 supplies the known cubic #P premise. Actual standalone verifier tested 1,369,076 complete derived-graph subsets across 81 source graphs, including shortest-path and induced-cube calculations. Finite tests are corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed new mathematical object is the explicit one-subdivision-plus-private-leaf bipartite gadget, inducing an exact bijection of all minimum dominating sets, an isomorphic slide/jump gamma reconfiguration graph, and a full induced-cube enumerator. Stronger general unconstrained realization and known simplex graph results are specifically carved out; their statements do not assert a bounded-degree, girth-six, linear-size bipartite construction with this polynomial transfer. The close 2016 generalized-corona subdivision paper was read in full and studies change thresholds, not the claimed entire set/reconfiguration profile. No directly covering claim was found in focused mathematical-record searches or related public-primary full texts. Residual unindexed/alternate terminology risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed literature may state the equivalent forced-private-pair gadget or an isomorphic subdivided-corona transformation, thereby covering the construction despite different terminology.
The known generic gamma-graph realization literature is much stronger without graph restrictions; bare existence or known simplex graph properties cannot be advertised as new.
The 2016 generalized-corona subdivision paper is close in operations; its full text did not cover this result, but other older graph-operation sources might.

value.rationale: The new restricted-realization theorem establishes a structural connection between minimum dominating sets in a high-girth bipartite graph and independent sets of an arbitrary source graph. It simultaneously transfers the full polynomial, all solutions and adjacency/move geometry, shortest distances, and cube counts. The construction is linear in source size, naturally sparse, and keeps maximum degree four on cubic graphs. Unlike routine single-value domination calculations or bare generic existence (known), it gives a useful universal explicit representation and parsimonious hardness under meaningful graph restrictions. Generalization to every source graph and implications for reconfiguration and counting motivate this particular transformation.
